items.text: We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.
items.why: States the paper's core architecture proposal.
items.plain: We propose a simple network called the Transformer that uses only attention mechanisms, completely avoiding recurrence and convolutions.

items.text: Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train.
items.why: Summarizes the main high-level translation result.
items.plain: Tests on two translation tasks show these models offer better quality, train much faster, and allow more parallel processing.

items.text: Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 Englishto-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU.
items.plain: Our model scores 28.4 BLEU on English-to-German translation, beating previous top results including combined models by over 2 BLEU.

items.text: On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the best models from the literature.
items.plain: On English-to-French translation, our single model sets a new top score of 41.8 BLEU after 3.5 days of training on eight GPUs at a fraction of typical costs.

items.text: We show that the Transformer generalizes well to other tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both with large and limited training data.
items.plain: The Transformer also works well on English sentence structure parsing with both large and small training sets.

items.text: In this work we propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and instead relying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output.
items.why: Declares the fundamental approach of the Transformer.
items.plain: We propose the Transformer, an architecture that drops recurrence and relies fully on attention to link inputs and outputs.

items.text: To the best of our knowledge, however, the Transformer is the first transduction model relying entirely on self-attention to compute representations of its input and output without using sequencealigned RNNs or convolution.
items.plain: To our knowledge, the Transformer is the first translation model using only self-attention without step-by-step recurrent networks or convolutions.

items.text: On the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, the big transformer model (Transformer (big) in Table 2) outperforms the best previously reported models (including ensembles) by more than 2.0 BLEU, establishing a new state-of-the-art BLEU score of 28.4.
items.plain: On English-to-German translation, our big model beats all previous models and combined ensembles by over 2.0 BLEU with a 28.4 score.

items.text: On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our big model achieves a BLEU score of 41.0, outperforming all of the previously published single models, at less than 1/4 the training cost of the previous state-of-the-art model.
items.plain: On English-to-French translation, our big model reaches a 41.0 BLEU score, beating previous single models at less than a quarter of the training cost.

items.text: In this work, we presented the Transformer, the first sequence transduction model based entirely on attention, replacing the recurrent layers most commonly used in encoder-decoder architectures with multi-headed self-attention.
items.why: Summarizes the overall contribution in the conclusion.
items.plain: We presented the Transformer, the first model relying entirely on self-attention instead of recurrent layers.
